r8c.rootCause:
r3 failed repeatedly for reasons that show in prompts.json. It is not the guide. The guide's lower box is 0.43 of the house width (computed from make-guides.mjs and building-kit's project), the same as r0, and r1 reached 0.43 on that same kind of guide in attempt 12.

1. Editing a painting makes the model redraw it. Attempt 9 was an edit of attempt 7 with the instruction "keep it where it is and as large as it is". The result had a house span of 786 px against 676 (Codex noted this itself, "expanded house footprint from 676 to 786"), and the walls grew less than the width did, so the ratio fell from about 0.40 to 0.37. Asking for three changes at once (light, crane, hose) gave the model licence to relayout.
2. A negative instruction does not remove a structure that is already in the picture. Attempt 7 already had the two-post portal. The prompt said "no second post and no cross beam", and attempt 9 kept both. The crane post sits at the far-left corner, and the near-corner riser still reads as a second support.
3. Numbers in text are not followed. "Gap at least half the door's height" and "0.45" were ignored. r1 only reached 0.43 on its third stacked correction (attempt 12). r3 never got a clean chain of consecutive corrections on one base. Attempt 9 edited attempt 7, then attempts 10 and 11 jumped back to the bare guide.
4. The r0-fitted reference pulls the model towards copying r0. Guide-based r3 attempts 6 and 10 both came back as r0 with the front on the lower left, while none of r1's guide-based attempts did. That is 2 of 5 r3 tries against 0 of 6 r1 tries.
5. Painting from the bare guide gives a poor camera and low walls: attempt 11 was 7.3 degrees off with walls 0.34, and attempt 10 had no verifiable camera.
6. The prompts grew: attempt 11's prompt is 8,420 characters of stacked "Correction:" paragraphs, including ones that contradict each other (edit a painting, then paint on the guide).

Attachments were not the problem. The image to edit was first and the references stayed within five. The guide is not wrong. The problem is the edit-of-attempt-7 approach, with too many changes at once and quantities given only in words.

c4d.rootCause: 1) The painter keeps the height but not the width. In raw returned pixels the painted stage is taller than r0, so the 62 px block-out worked on height. But its pier feet span 794, 737 and 725 px against r0's 636 and the guide plinth's 631, which is 26, 17 and 15 percent wider than the plinth. The fit scales every picture by that foot span, so a wider stage comes out lower: this is the whole height shortfall for r1, and part of it for r3 and r2. Height therefore swings with the painter's pier spread, from 1.06 to 1.37 across the nine attempts, and the window is 1.318 to 1.611, so a pass by luck is about one in four, before the plan and camera tests. 2) The guide has a square plan and only a thin flat plinth with no piers. The stage's real plan is 1 to 1.364 with six piers, so the painter reinvents the proportions: r1 lengthened the long side 36 percent, r3 widened the short side 32 percent (plan 1.069, nearly square). Nothing in the guide pins the pier feet. 3) Camera drift is a side effect of the same freedom: elevation 3.5 to 9.2 degrees and turn up to 8 degrees. 4) The winch in r3 sits mid-wall rather than at the near end, as the prompt asked; the painter drifts back towards r0's layout. A direct check shows r0 mirrored horizontally already passes the geometry tests: box.top 281.5, height 1.472, plan 1.365, camera 1.4 degrees (turn -0.7). This is why a seed built from r0 should work where a grey block does not. One caveat: my 631 px plinth width assumes the 1024 guide maps to the 1254 returns at 1.2246, which the overlays support.
nextSteps: Core decision on r2: restore raw/fuel_stop-a0-r2-attempt-8.png (byte-identical to the Codex return) and either run the tool's camera-only repaint from its own fitted self, or accept it as a documented 3.5 degree camera exception for Art to finish. Amber 26 px fitted is capped at packing.

Fix for r1 and r3, a different method (recommended): Art builds the seed from r0, not from the grey block. Mirror r0 horizontally; this measures height 1.472, plan 1.365, camera 1.4 degrees, so every geometry test passes. For r1, erase the chute, winch and chain, and relight the two walls so the lower-left is lighter (a mirror reverses r0's light). For r3, keep the chute, move the winch and chain from the far end to the near (bottom) end, and relight. Use the seed as the edit-from picture for the painter with the prompt 'relight and tidy only; keep every silhouette, pier and post where it is'. The painter then changes almost nothing geometric and the fit has little to shrink.

Fix as a guide change, if a painter-only route is kept: replace the square block on a thin plinth with r0's actual plan. Draw the block oblong so the foot split is 0.577 : 0.423 for r1 and r3 (long side lower-left) and 0.423 : 0.577 for r2, i.e. s.x = w.x + 0.577 x (e.x - w.x) on the same 2:1 lines. Add six stone-coloured pier stubs at the exact foot positions, and use the existing 62 px block height. The pier span is the quantity the painter keeps inflating and the fit measures. Also add 'do not widen the piers beyond the stubs' to the Correction.

Prompt change: stop asking for 'the height'. Ask the painter to keep the grey block's width and the pier stubs, and drop the long text about legs. Keep at most three attempts per view and judge the foot span (pier span within 5 percent of 631 px in a 1254 return) before running the full fit. A span over 700 px is a sure low result and should not be recorded as an attempt.

r2 is the only view worth another painter round; for r1 and r3, spend the next try on the composite seed instead of more painter attempts. If Core prefers not to use Art compositing, r3 attempt 9 could be an Art finishing job only with a large shear and a plan stretch, which I do not recommend.
